title: How to Buy a House in Saudi Arabia: A 2026 First-Time Buyer’s Guide
text:
There is a particular kind of anxiety that comes with wanting something you don’t fully understand yet. You want a home. You want the specific, permanent feeling of a place that is yours, not your landlord’s, not temporary in the way that rented things always feel temporary, even when you’ve lived somewhere for years.
You want to know 
how to buy a house in Saudi Arabia
. And yet the process seems designed, at every turn, to make that want feel slightly out of reach, but it doesn’t have to be.
If you’re looking at 
houses for sale in Saudi Arabia
 for the first time — particularly 
homes in Riyadh
, where the market is moving fast and the options are genuinely overwhelming — this guide is for you.
Not the version of you who already knows what an LTV ratio is, but the version sitting at your phone at midnight, wondering where to even begin.
How to Buy a House in Saudi Arabia; A First Time Buyer’s Guide
What You Need to Know Before Buying a Home in Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia’s real estate market in 2026 is not what it was a decade ago. The government has been deliberate about expanding homeownership, making it easier for you to 
buy a house in Saudi Arabia
 in 2026.
Key Market Facts
Homeownership rate increased from 
47% in 2016
 to 
66.24% in 2025
Vision 2030 targets 
70% homeownership by 2030
Government-backed programmes now support first-time buyers
Mortgage access and housing subsidies are more accessible than ever
The infrastructure built around that ambition is real. There are programmes, subsidies, and platforms that didn’t exist before.
Knowing 
how to buy a house in Saudi Arabia
 means understanding that the process is more supported than most people assume.
Step 1: Check Your Eligibility
Before searching for 
apartments for sale in Riyadh
 or 
villas for sale in Riyadh
, you need to understand your eligibility status to 
buy a house in Saudi Arabia.
For Saudi Nationals
Eligible for government-backed financing through the 
Real Estate Development Fund (REDF)
 via 
Sakani
Maximum LTV ratio of 
90%
 for first-home buyers
Down payment can be as low as 
10%
First-time buyers purchasing homes worth 
SAR 1 million or less
 may qualify for 
RETT exemption
For Expat Residents
Foreign nationals can now 
buy a house in Saudi Arabia
 in designated zones under the new 2026 foreign ownership law
Expat LTV is generally capped at 
75–80%
Most lenders require 
20–35% down payment
Valid 
Iqama
 and proof of stable employment are required
Ownership in 
Makkah and Madinah
 remains restricted
Important Tip
If you’re a Saudi citizen buying your first home, registering on the

title: King Salman Park Riyadh: Real Estate Impact, Vision 2030 & Investment Guide 2026
text:
The development of King Salman PaA Guide to hork Riyadh is shape shifting realestate in the city. It Doesnt simply exist as a green space; it fundamentally alters perceptions, property values, and how investors think about where to build.
This guide will help you further understand how the park is shaping Riyadh and hi=ow the project aligns with 2030 vision.
What Is King Salman Park Riyadh?
King Salman Park Riyadh is one of the world’s largest urban parks. Covering more than 16 square kilometers, it is set to become the largest urban park in the world, built on the former site of Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport.
The park is bigger than what the mind can fathom. To put it into perspective; it is more than eleven times the size of London’s Hyde Park (1.4 km²) and nearly five times the size of New York’s Central Park (3.4 km²).
King Salman Park was officially launched by the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman Bin Abdulaziz, on 
19 March 2019
, as part of broader urban development initiatives aligned with 
Saudi Vision 2030
.
King Salman Park Opening Date: Current Timeline
Although the timeline has changed, as is common with such mega projects, the park is expected to open its first phase to visitors in 2026 with major sections of green space, walkways, and initial facilities expected to be accessible by then. Full completion is currently targeted for 
2027
, with additional phases opening progressively.
This timeline matters significantly for real estate investors. Properties marketed around near-term opening dates tend to command premium valuations which can compress if delivery timelines extend further.
King Salman Park Riyadh
Vision 2030 and King Salman Park: A Strategic Alignment
King Salman Park aims to improve the quality of life in the city in direct alignment with 
Saudi Vision 2030
‘s goals of building a vibrant, healthy society and raising Riyadh’s global ranking as a liveable metropolis. The park is not an isolated vanity project; it is central to Saudi Arabia’s broader economic diversification strategy, which seeks to reduce the country’s dependence on oil revenues by developing tourism, culture, and residential infrastructure.
The 
King Salman Park Foundation (KSPF)
 is responsible for overseeing the implementation, operation, and investment management of the park.
Core Features of King Salman Park Riyadh
The park integrates multiple components across its 16 km² footprint:
Green Space:
 More than 11 km² of landscaped areas featuring approximately one million trees
Transport Connectivity:
 Five Riyadh Metro stations — four on the Green Line and one on the Red Line — plus 10 stations on the Riyadh Bus Network
Cultural Hub:
 The Royal Arts Complex, encompassing eight museums including an Aviation Museum, Saudi Society Museum, Museum of World Cultures, Astronomy and Space Museum, Science Museum, Museum of Plants, Virtual Reality Museum, and Architecture Museum
Walkability:
 A circular pedestrian walkway extending over 7 km
Residential Component:
 The park will include approximately 12,000 housing units within its boundaries
Real Estate Impact: What the Data Shows
Property Value Premiums
Analysis of major infrastructure projects in comparable urban markets shows a 
5–15% price premium
 typically emerging at project announcement, with an 
additional 10–20% uplift
 as construction completes and facilities become operational. These premiums reflect both investor confidence and genuine lifestyle improvements driven by proximity to green space and amenities.
It is worth noting these are market patterns, not guaranteed outcomes. Premiums can compress if supply outpaces demand or if delivery delays extend timelines further.
Investment Activity
The private sector response to King Salman Park Riyadh has been substantial:
A mixed-use real estate development project 
valued at approximately SAR 4 billion
 will comprise over 1,500 residential units — including apartments and townhouses overlooking the park — alongside office and retail space
The King Salman Park Foundation established a 
SAR 3.8 billion (~USD 1 billion) fund
 in partnership with Ajdan Real Estate and SEDCO Capital, targeting residential, commercial, and hospitality components
Market Valuation
In 
July 2024
, real estate consultancy Knight Frank valued King Salman Park at 
USD 9.4 billion
. This, along side infrastructure improvements, makes the surrounding area a promising realestate
 investment oppurtunity. 
Qiddiya Saudi Arabia: Complementary Development
King Salman Park
 does not operate in isolation. Alongside the 
New Murabba downtown district
, 
Qiddiya Saudi Arabia
, and the 
Diriyah Gate cultural destination
, it forms part of a concentrated cluster of megaprojects actively reshaping Riyadh’s urban landscape.
Qiddiya Saudi Arabia
, positioned as a major entertainment destination to the southwest of Riyadh, creates synergistic effects; properties positioned with accessibility to both 
Qiddiya
 and 
King Salman Park
 benefit from the concentrated economic activity each attracts. Together, these projects represent a deliberate effort to diversify Riyadh’s urban identity beyond its traditional commercial core.
Qiddiya
How Real Estate Markets Actually Respond
The real estate market doesn’t respond to parks as abstract amenities. Practically, the dynamics work like this:
Accessibility Premium:
 Central location with metro connectivity typically adds 5–15% at announcement
Construction Premium:
 An additional 10–20% uplift tends to accumulate as opening approaches and uncertainty reduces
Lifestyle Signal:
 Significant public investment in livability signals to both residents and investors that Riyadh is prioritising long-term quality of life
Employment Creation:
 Construction phases and ongoing park operations create sustained economic activity in surrounding districts
Large-scale urban parks have a well-documented history of increasing surrounding property values in comparable cities. Residential and commercial districts adjacent to King Salman Park are positioned to become prime Riyadh real estate — provided demand keeps pace with the significant supply additions planned across the capital.
Beyond Speculation: Real Quality-of-Life Factors
The appeal is not purely financial. King Salman Park Riyadh delivers measurable quality-of-life improvements that create persistent, genuine demand:
Pedestrian networks reduce car dependency in a city historically designed around vehicle use
Extensive green space provides meaningful mitigation of Riyadh’s desert heat
Cultural facilities create community gathering points currently underrepresented in the city
Mixed-use design enables residents to live, work, and recreate within the same district
These factors create durable demand that can sustain property values long after initial speculative premiums have normalised.
King Salman Park Riyadh: Investment Considerations
The opportunity is real, but balanced assessment requires acknowledging both sides:
Upside:
 Properties with strong accessibility — particularly metro proximity — to King Salman Park Riyadh are well-positioned to appreciate as:
The first phase opens in 2026
Additional phases complete through 2027 and beyond
Amenities activate and attract permanent residents
Commercial demand stabilises around the park’s cultural and retail anchors
Downside:
 Some current pricing reflects speculative optimism that may not fully materialise. Delivery delays are common in megaprojects globally. Riyadh is simultaneously delivering New Murabba (100,000+ housing units), Diriyah Gate, expanded metro services, and numerous other large-scale developments — meaning housing supply is rising significantly across the city. The critical variable across all of these is the relationship between housing supply and population-driven demand. Riyadh’s population is growing, but the volume of units being developed simultaneously across these megaprojects is substantial.
Final Perspective: King Salman Park Riyadh and Urban Evolution
King Salman Park Riyadh represents something beyond a real estate investment thesis. It signals that a major Middle Eastern capital is making a generational bet on livability, cultural depth, and sustainable urban design — a meaningful shift for a city that has historically been car-centric and commercially focused.
Whether you’re an investor or a future resident, this commitment reshapes which neighbourhoods become desirable and why. The park’s real estate impact will ultimately be measured in two ways: the price premiums that materialise, and the actual quality-of-life improvements that justify and sustain those premiums over time.

King Salman Park is expected to open its first phase to visitors in 2026, with major green spaces, walkways, and initial facilities accessible by then. Full completion is currently targeted for 2027, with additional phases opening progressively.

King Salman Park is nearly five times the size of New York’s Central Park, which covers 3.4 square kilometers. At over 16 square kilometers, it is also more than eleven times larger than London’s Hyde Park, making it one of the largest urban parks in the world.
How does King Salman Park affect Riyadh real estate prices?
Properties near King Salman Park are expected to see a 5–15% price premium at the project announcement stage, with an additional 10–20% uplift as construction completes and facilities open. What is the King Salman Park Foundation?
The King Salman Park Foundation (KSPF) is the official body responsible for overseeing the implementation, operation, and investment management of King Salman Park. It has established a SAR 3.8 billion fund in partnership with Ajdan Real Estate and SEDCO Capital to develop residential, commercial, and hospitality components within and around the park.
How is King Salman Park connected to Saudi Vision 2030?
King Salman Park is a central pillar of Saudi Vision 2030’s goal to build a vibrant, liveable society and reduce dependence on oil revenues. It supports the Vision’s targets around quality of life, cultural development, tourism, and urban diversification, positioning Riyadh as a globally competitive metropolis.

King Salman Park presents a significant real estate opportunity, particularly for properties with strong metro connectivity and proximity to the park. However, investors should weigh the upside — phased openings from 2026, cultural amenities, and infrastructure investment — against risks including delivery delays and rising housing supply across Riyadh from simultaneous megaprojects like New Murabba and Diriyah Gate.
What facilities will King Salman Park include?
King Salman Park will include over 11 square kilometers of green space, approximately one million trees, eight museums within the Royal Arts Complex, a 7 km circular pedestrian walkway, five Riyadh Metro stations, 10 bus network stations, around 12,000 residential units, and a range of retail and hospitality facilities.
Which metro lines serve King Salman Park? 
King Salman Park is served by five Riyadh Metro stations — four on the Green Line and one on the Red Line — as well as 10 stations on the Riyadh Bus Network, making it one of the most transit-accessible destinations in the city.

title: Top 2026 Tips for Foreigners Buying Property in Saudi Arabia
text:
Are you 
foreigners buying property in Saudi Arabia
? If the answer to that question is yes, the good news is that Saudi Arabia is opening its doors to foreign investment to align with Vision 2030; this initiative is supported by the newly enacted laws adopted by the Saudi government to encourage foreign investment. 
Starting January 2026, the Saudi government significantly broadened foreigners’ access to property ownership, contrary to the previous law (the Golden Visa), which allowed only a limited category of foreign residents to own property.
Are foreigners buying property in Saudi Arabia?
To answer that question, we must examine the laws enacted by the Saudi government.
Foreign residents and investors are now eligible to buy property in Saudi Arabia, thanks to the newly enacted law. Below are the key variables to 
buying property in Saudi Arabia
, subject to conditions set by the 
General Real Estate Authority (REGA)
: 
Property location: 
ownership is designated to specific cities, such as Riyadh and Jeddah, with more restrictive rules for buying property in Makkah and Madinah
Residency status
: foreign residents may also own one residential property outside designated zones for personal use
Entity type
: foreign companies may acquire real estate necessary for business operations or employee housing, subject to applicable licensing requirements
Freehold vs. Usufruct Rights: 
The new law allows both freehold ownership and usufruct rights. Usufruct differs from freehold (which completely transfers ownership) because it allows benefiting from the property for a certain period without transferring ownership. 
Regulatory Approvals: 
Certain categories of foreign residents require approval or registration from the relevant authorities, such as the 
Ministry of Interior
 or REGA
Can foreigners buy property in Saudi Arabia?
What you should do next:
Verify your residency status:
 Ensure your Iqama has at least six months of validity.
Consult the Ministry of Justice:
 Review the latest circulars on foreign ownership zones.
Use Wasalt:
 Browse 
verified listings
 to gauge current market prices in your target city.
Real Estate and Residency: The Foreign Property-Owner Pathway
Foreigners can buy property for the long term if their investment is at least SAR 4,000,000 (approximately USD 1,070,000) through 
the Golden Visa
.
The property must be residential, completed and ready to occupy, free from mortgages or liens, and independently valued by an accredited professional registered with 
TAQEEM
, the Saudi Authority for Accredited Valuers
Residency under this pathway remains valid as long as the applicant continues to own the qualifying property. Premium residency holders can leave and re-enter Saudi Arabia without needing a separate exit or re-entry visa, which is a significant upgrade from the traditional Iqama sponsorship system.
Why Investors Are Looking at Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia has been attracting more investors through the Vision 2030 initiative, which is preparing the
 country for strong non-oil GDP growth, rapid urbanization, and large-scale infrastructure, with 
Riyadh
 at the center of 
investment opportunities. 
Giga-Projects and Development Scale
Saudi Arabia is attracting investments with its large-scale projects, such as: 
NEOM
Qiddiya
The Red Sea Project
The Diriyah Gate development
NEOM
Understanding the Real Estate Transaction Tax (RETT)
Saudi Arabia introduced 
the Real Estate Transaction Tax (RETT)
 at a rate of 5% in October 2020, replacing the previous 15% VAT on real estate transactions. This flat 5% rate applies to the total value of real estate transactions regardless of the property’s ownership, type, use, or condition, covering residential, commercial, and industrial properties.
 
RETT is calculated based on the total value of the agreed transaction at the date of disposal, which should not be less than fair market value, and is payable to 
ZATCA
 on the date of the transaction—i.e., the date of its notarization.
One important nuance for 
foreigners buying property in Saudi Arabia
: the foreign ownership framework adds a 5% RETT plus an additional 5% foreign ownership-related fee, which can round up to 10% of the purchase price. Taxes on the property are levied under RATT rather than VAT, which is now applied to services related to the deal, such as brokerage fees, legal work, and valuation services.
ZATCA
Conclusion
Foreigners buying property in Saudi Arabia
 are subject to regulations enforced by the Saudi Arabian government, and these regulations have been optimized to increase the chances for 
foreigners buying property in Saudi Arabia
 and making investments in Saudi Arabia much easier than in 2020.
Frequently Asked Questions
Are foreigners buying property in Saudi Arabia?
Yes. Foreign residents with a valid Iqama can own one residential property for personal use, subject to Ministry of Interior approval. Non-Muslims cannot own property in Makkah or Madinah.
What is the RETT for foreigners buying property in Saudi Arabia?
A flat 5% tax on the total property transaction value, paid through the ZATCA portal before the deed is notarized. Additional foreign ownership fees may bring total government charges to around 10%.
Can I buy property in Saudi Arabia without living there?
Yes. The 2026 law allows non-residents to buy within designated zones. However, purchasing below the SAR 4 million threshold will not qualify you for residency.
Is it better to buy or rent in Riyadh as an expat?
It depends on your length of stay and financial situation. Buying suits long-term residents; renting suits those staying short-term. Factor in legal fees and ownership surcharges before deciding, and seek independent financial advice.
What happens to my property if I permanently leave Saudi Arabia?
You keep ownership, but managing property remotely is complex. Registering a Power of Attorney (PoA) with the Ministry of Justice allows a trusted representative to manage or sell it on your behalf.
Where are foreigners buying property in Saudi Arabia?
Designated zones in major cities like Riyadh and Jeddah, and development projects such as NEOM, Qiddiya, and the Red Sea Project. REGA publishes the official list of approved ownership zones.

The relationship between DarGlobal and Wasalt has two parts. 1) Common parent link: DarGlobal (Dar Global) is the international property arm of Saudi developer Dar Al Arkan (The National, June 2025). Wasalt is described on its corporate pages as a joint venture between Dar Al Arkan and Quara Holding, a technology startup incubator. So both companies are connected to Dar Al Arkan. Ziad El Chaar is CEO of DarGlobal and Chairman of Wasalt. 2) Commercial partnership: in April 2025 DarGlobal announced a partnership with Wasalt under which Trump Tower Jeddah is advertised and listed on Wasalt's website and app to reach investors and property seekers across Saudi Arabia (DarGlobal press release, 16 April 2025).
This note was written by hand from public sources: the DarGlobal press release, The National, Gulf Tech News and Wasalt's public corporate description.
